Chapter 1
Executive Summary

A Case for Regular Recognition

This dossier sets out the regularity of origin, constitutional foundations, and international recognitions of the National Grand Lodge of Greece (NGLG). Established in 1986 by six regularly warranted Craft Lodges, the NGLG has preserved an unbroken record of constitutional continuity, observance of the Ancient Landmarks, and sovereign self-government across nearly four decades of uninterrupted operation.

It is presented in response to enquiries from fraternal Grand Lodges considering recognition, addressing questions of doctrine, governance, jurisdiction, and coexistence with the Grand Lodge of Greece.

Chapter 3
Principles details

Faith, the Sacred Law & the Landmarks

Regularity of origin

i.e. each Grand Lodge shall have been established lawfully by a duly recognized Grand Lodge or by three or more regularly constituted Lodges.

That a belief in the G.A.O.T.U.

and His revealed will shall be an essential qualification for membership.

Volume of the Sacred Law

That all Initiates shall take their Obligation on or in full view of the open Volume of the Sacred Law, by which is meant the revelation from above which is binding on the conscience of the particular individual who is being initiated.

Masons are only men

That the membership of the Grand Lodge and individual Lodges shall be composed exclusively of those who were made Masons as men; and that each Grand Lodge shall have no Masonic association of any kind with bodies which make women Masons.

Sovereign jurisdiction over the Lodges under its control

That the Grand Lodge shall have sovereign jurisdiction over the Lodges under its control; i.e. that it shall be a responsible, independent, self-governing organization, with sole and undisputed authority over the Craft or Symbolic Degrees (Entered Apprentice, Fellow Craft, and Master Mason) within its Jurisdiction; and shall not in any way be subject to, or divide such authority with, a Supreme Council or other Power claiming any control or supervision over those degrees.

Volume of the Sacred Law, the Square, and the Compasses

That the three Great Lights of Freemasonry (namely, the Volume of the Sacred Law, the Square, and the Compasses) shall always be exhibited when the Grand Lodge or its subordinate Lodges are at work, the chief of these being the Volume of the Sacred Law.

No discussion of religion and politics within the Lodge

That the discussion of religion and politics within the Lodge shall be strictly prohibited.

Antient Landmarks

That the principles of the Antient Landmarks, customs, and usages of the Craft shall be strictly observed.

Chapter 4
PRINCIPLES ON 4 & 7

Membership & Fraternal Conduct

Admission of Free Men of Good Character

Membership is restricted exclusively to free men of good character and reputation. The NGLG does not admit women, mixed membership, or maintain relations with mixed, feminine, or irregular Masonic organisations.

No Political or Sectarian Discussion

Partisan politics and sectarian religion are strictly prohibited within the Lodges. The NGLG firmly upholds the Lodge as a place of harmony, fraternity, and moral instruction, free from controversy.

Chapter 5
PRINCIPLES ON 5

Sovereignty & Independence

Principle of sovereign and independent Masonic jurisdiction.

The National Grand Lodge of Greece (NGLG) fully complies with the principle of sovereign and independent Masonic jurisdiction. It exercises exclusive and undivided authority over its constituent Lodges and the three Symbolic Degrees — Entered Apprentice, Fellow Craft, and Master Mason — within its jurisdiction.

Chapter 6
FOUNDATION. PRINCIPLE 1

A Regular Origin — 7 June 1986

7 June
1986
Athens, Greece
6 Lodges · ~250 Brethren
Presided by the late RWBro. William R. J. Eve, Past Grand Deacon, UGLE — first Deputy Grand Master of the NGLG.

Six regularly constituted Craft Lodges — acting unanimously in the exercise of their inherent Masonic rights — withdrew from the jurisdiction of the Grand Lodge of Greece to constitute an independent, sovereign Grand Lodge, in accordance with the Ancient Landmarks and the universally accepted principles of Regular Freemasonry.

This was not a schism over doctrine or ritual, but a constitutional response to disagreements over governance and the future direction of Greek Craft Freemasonry. The founding Lodges possessed valid Masonic warrants, an established succession of duly initiated, passed and raised members, and an unquestioned origin within Regular Craft Freemasonry — comfortably exceeding the minimum of three regularly constituted Lodges required to constitute a new Grand Lodge.

The soundness of their decision subsequently received significant institutional confirmation. In 1993, only seven years after the establishment of the National Grand Lodge of Greece, the United Grand Lodge of England withdrew its recognition from the Grand Lodge of Greece and formally recognised the National Grand Lodge of Greece instead. This important development provided strong international confirmation that the NGLG’s origin, constitution and Masonic standing satisfied the fundamental requirements of Regular Craft Freemasonry.

The Constitution adopted was substantially based upon the 1984 Book of Constitutions of the United Grand Lodge of England, expressly incorporating the 1929 Basic Principles for Grand Lodge Recognition.

Chapter 8
History

Chain of Recognition — 1986 to 2026

1986

The NGLG is founded in Athens by six regularly constituted Lodges.

1993

Recognised by the United Grand Lodge of England. (UGLE)

1994

Recognised by the Grand Lodge of Ireland (3 October).

1995

Recognised by the Grand Lodge of Scotland (4 May) — all three Home Grand Lodges now in amity.

1999

UGLE transfers recognition to the Grand Lodge of Greece to encourage dialogue — expressly stating the NGLG remains Regular. Ireland & Scotland maintain recognition, uninterrupted to this day.

Today

102 mutual recognitions worldwide; active participation in the World Conference of Regular Grand Lodges and the European Conferences.

Chapter 9
Coexistence

Two Regular Grand Lodges, One Nation

The NGLG does not claim exclusive territorial sovereignty over all Craft Freemasonry in Greece. Since 1999, the practical reality within Regular Freemasonry has been one of jurisdictional coexistence between the NGLG and the Grand Lodge of Greece (GLG) — a position acknowledged by numerous Regular Grand Lodges that today maintain fraternal relations with both.

There is no bilateral treaty between the NGLG and the GLG governing coexistence; the situation has developed through the independent recognition policies of individual Regular Grand Lodges. The NGLG exercises exclusive jurisdiction over its own Constitution, Lodges, and members — consistent with practice recognised throughout the regular Masonic world.

Key Distinction

Recognition is a sovereign, diplomatic decision by one Grand Lodge concerning Masonic intercourse. Regularity concerns whether a Grand Lodge conforms to the established principles of Regular Freemasonry — the two are not the same. UGLE concerns the National Grand Lodge of Greece as a uninterrupted Continious Regular Grand Lodge.

UGLE's published historical record describes the 1999 decision as one to withdraw recognition "despite its continuing regularity."

Education
Conference of Worshipful Masters
Every year, a dedicated Conference of Worshipful Masters is held in Athens, bringing together the Worshipful Masters of the Symbolic Lodges. The Conference features lectures, presentations and discussions on lodge administration, leadership, ethics, Masonic conduct and the responsibilities of the Chair. Its purpose is to strengthen the knowledge and abilities of each Worshipful Master, helping him to govern his Lodge efficiently, exercise sound judgement, preserve Masonic principles and lead his Brethren with dignity, fairness and wisdom. It is conceived not merely as an annual meeting, but as a continuing school of Masonic leadership, dedicated to improving both the administrative effectiveness and the moral quality of the Master’s service.
Grand Meetings
Annual, Semi Annual , Election
The Annual Meeting is held on the third Saturday of May, and the Semi-Annual Meeting on the third Saturday of December. Every five years, during an election year, an additional Grand Meeting is held to elect the Grand Master and the Grand Treasurer.

Chapter 14
Governance

Administrative & Masonic Structure

Supreme authority is vested in the Grand Lodge, presided over by the democratically elected Most Worshipful Grand Master, assisted by Grand Officers and constitutional committees. The Grand Lodge governs 83 Lodges across 5 Provinces and 1 District, exercising exclusive authority over the three Craft Degrees.

General Board Of Purpose & General Boad of Charity

Administratively separate, governing only their own additional degrees — none exercises authority over the Craft or the NGLG's internal government:

  • Supreme Grand Chapter of Royal Arch Masons of Greece
  • Grand Lodge of Mark Master Masons of Greece
  • Grand Council of Royal and Select Masters
  • Great Priory of Greece · Grand Imperial Conclave
  • Province of Knight Masons · Order of the Secret Monitor
  • Supreme Council 33°
5 + 1
Provinces & one District
Headquartered in Athens, supported by the Offices of the Grand Secretary and Grand Chancellor, with committees for governance, finance, charity, external relations and education. NGLG holds two business meetings a year, known as Semi Annual each December and Annual Communication each May. Only the year of elections (every 5 years there is an extra Communication in March) NGLG, its Lodges and members operates to a rule book, known as The Book of Constitutions, which was first published in 1986 and is based on the Book of Constitution of UGLE.
No Supreme Council of AASR 33 or appendant body exercises authority over Craft governance.

Chapter 17
Conclusion

Four Pillars of Regularity

The NGLG's regularity of origin rests upon four clear and cumulative foundations.

1

Lawful Establishment

By six regularly constituted Lodges — exceeding the minimum of three required to found a Grand Lodge.

2

Unbroken Lineage

The founding Lodges carried uninterrupted regular Masonic lineage, with valid warrants and succession.

3

Constitutional Fidelity

Continuous adoption and observance of the universally accepted principles of Regular Freemasonry.

4

Enduring Recognition

Historical and continuing recognition by long-established Regular Grand Lodges, including Ireland and Scotland.
